newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malay party reshuffles some leadership posts.
newsitem.headline: Malay party reshuffles some leadership posts.

text.p: Malaysia's ruling party made several key leadership changes in its highest decision-making body, but Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said no Cabinet reshuffle was in the works, local newspapers said on Friday.

At a news conference after midnight on Thursday, Mahathir Mohamad, president of the United Malays National Organisation (UMNO), said Supreme Council Secretary-General Mohamed Rahmat was being replaced by Tourism Minister Sabbaruddin Chik.
Mohamed Rahmat, information minister, had held the post for eight years.
Mahathir also said Terengganu state official Mohamed Yusof Noor would be the information chief for the council, replacing Hussein Ahmad.
Both Mohamed Rahmat and Hussein Ahmad, an UMNO leader in Kelantan state, were instead appointed members of the council.

"We feel that no one is permanent in UMNO, sometimes he has to go because he is not chosen or not appointed or for other reasons like ill-health, lack of interest or resignation and so forth." the Bernama news agency quoted Mahathir as saying.

The council also chose not to appoint as members two ministers who lost in the UMNO party polls in October. Muhyiddin Yassin, youth and sports minister, and Annuar Musa, rural development minister, were left off the list.
Positions in the Supreme Council are closely watched because members are often given jobs in the government.
Asked whether their positions as ministers would be jeopardised, Mahathir said: "Not affected, we don't have a Cabinet reshuffle...it is not easy to reshuffle."
UMNO is the dominant party in the ruling National Front coaliation that has held power since Malaysia gained independence from Britain in 1957.
As expected, Mahathir and Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim were returned unopposed as president and deputy president of the council for the 1996-1999 term.

The council appointed eight new members, including four who had lost their UMNO general election races in October. Among them was International Trade and Industry Minister Rafidah Aziz, who lost her post as head of UMNO's women's wing in October.
Other new members are Defence Minister Syed Hamid Syed Jaafar Albar, and Ramli Ngah Talib, chief minister of Perak state. Both lost in the UMNO vice presidential race.
The council also appointed Isa Samad, Negri Sembilan state chief minister, who lost his bid for the UMNO youth leadership.
The council also kept Daim Zainuddin, an economic adviser to the government and an influential financial figure, as its treasurer-general.
The Supreme Council has 45 members, of which 25 are elected and the rest are appointed. Mahathir said he would fill two of the appointed posts later.
